edges.description: DSP desmosomal disruption can also manifest as variably present cutaneous findings in heterozygous carriers.
Desmoplakin is also a component of hair follicle and epidermal desmosomes; haploinsufficiency is associated with curly hair in a large fraction of carriers.
Myocyte injury and the inflammatory response it provokes present clinically as episodic myocarditis-like hot phases.
Each episode of acute myocardial injury presents with chest pain and troponin release despite normal coronary arteries.
Replacement fibrosis of the left ventricular wall is visualized as late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI.
Progressive myocardial replacement and remodeling produce left-dominant or biventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction.
The arrhythmogenic substrate manifests as frequent ventricular ectopy.

nodes.description: Progressive fibrofatty replacement of myocardium creates substrates for re-entrant ventricular arrhythmias. DSP cardiomyopathy carries a high risk of sudden cardiac death, which can occur even before overt structural disease is detected. Episodic inflammatory "hot phases" mimicking myocarditis may trigger arrhythmic events.

nodes.description: Desmoplakin is the most abundant protein in desmosomes, linking the transmembranous desmosomal cadherins to the intermediate filament network. Heterozygous truncating variants in DSP lead to haploinsufficiency, weakening the desmosomal complex in cardiomyocytes. The left ventricle is frequently involved early, distinguishing DSP cardiomyopathy from classic right-dominant ARVC.
